# Bug report

The test suite in this repository fails.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
F                                                                        [100%]
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
__________________________ test_expiry_at_exactly_ttl __________________________
    def test_expiry_at_exactly_ttl():
        c = Clock()
        cache = TTLCache(2, 10.0, c)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        c.t = 10.0
>       assert cache.get("a") is None
E       AssertionError: assert 1 is None
E        +  where 1 = get('a')
E        +    where get = <solution.core.TTLCache object at 0x...>.get
tests/test_public.py:14: AssertionError
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/test_public.py::test_expiry_at_exactly_ttl - AssertionError: ass...
1 failed in <duration>
```

Fix the source so that the suite passes.

Constraints:
- Do not modify anything under `tests/`.
- Do not add new dependencies; the standard library is all that is available.
- Keep the public API of the `solution` package unchanged: `TTLCache`.

     def _expired(self, ts) -> bool:
-        return self.clock() - ts > self.ttl

summary: I changed one file, `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (1 passed). The bug was an off-by-one in `TTLCache._expired`: it used `clock() - ts > ttl`, so an entry was still treated as live at exactly `ttl` seconds after insertion, and only expired after that. I changed it to `>=` so an entry expires the moment its age reaches `ttl`. Every expiry check in the cache goes through `_expired`: lookups in `get`, the live-entry count in `put` that decides whether to evict, and `_purge`. So all of them now use the same boundary, rather than only the case the visible test covers. One thing I noticed but left alone, since the issue doesn't mention it: `put` only clears out expired entries when the cache is full of live ones, and `__len__` counts expired entries that haven't been removed yet. That means `len(cache)` can go above `capacity`.
